originalTitle: US stocks today: S&P 500 and Nasdaq end higher on cool inflation data, solid bank earnings
simplifiedContent: Here's a simple explanation of the stock market news: The US stock market had a good day, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq indexes going up. This happened because investors were happy with some new information: inflation (the rate at which prices are rising) was not as high as expected in June, and some big banks like JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs had strong earnings. This made investors feel more positive, even though there are worries about problems in the Middle East. As a result, investors now think it's less likely that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates soon, which also helped the market.

originalTitle: US derivatives regulator blocks Kalshi from canceling Michigan trades despite court order
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: a company called Kalshi was ordered by a court in Michigan to cancel some trades, but the US derivatives regulator stepped in and stopped them from doing so. This is significant because it shows a disagreement between federal authorities and state governments over how to regulate certain types of trades, known as prediction markets. These trades are similar to sports betting, but are considered financial transactions by the federal government. The regulator's decision highlights a bigger issue about who has the power to make rules about these types of trades. This clash could impact the future of companies like Kalshi that offer event-based trading platforms.

originalTitle: Why IBM shares crashed 26%: CEO Arvind Krishna highlights customer spending shifts towards AI
simplifiedContent: IBM's stock price dropped 26% because the company's recent financial results were not as good as people expected. This happened because customers are changing how they spend their money, and many are now prioritizing artificial intelligence (AI) technology. According to IBM's CEO, Arvind Krishna, customers are focusing on getting the hardware they need for AI, which was in short supply. The company also made some mistakes and had problems with one of its main businesses, which contributed to the poor results. This matters because it shows that IBM is having trouble keeping up with changes in the market, which can affect the company's future success.

originalTitle: Multibagger Signature Global shares to be in focus on Wednesday after Q1 pre-sales rise 25% QoQ
simplifiedContent: Signature Global, a company listed on the stock market, will be closely watched on Wednesday due to its recent sales update. The company's sales for the first quarter of the current financial year (FY27) were ₹1,970 crore, which is 25% lower than the same time last year, but 25% higher than the previous quarter. This increase from the previous quarter is attributed to the launch of a new project called Tonino Lamborghini Residences. This news is important because it could affect the company's stock price, making it a key thing to watch on Wednesday. The change in sales could impact investor interest in the company.

originalTitle: Gold, silver prices today: Comex gold and silver rebound as softer US inflation eases Fed rate hike fears
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the prices of gold and silver went up on July 14th because inflation in the US wasn't as high as expected. This makes investors less worried that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates, which is good for gold and silver. As a result, the price of gold rose to $4,112 and silver rose to $60. This matters because when inflation is lower, investors are more likely to buy gold and silver, which can push their prices up. The rising tensions in the Middle East also supported the increase in gold and silver prices.

originalTitle: Govt reviews fresh bids for IDBI Bank as stake sale process gathers pace
simplifiedContent: The Indian government and LIC, a big insurance company, own a large part of IDBI Bank. They want to sell about 60.72% of the bank, which includes transferring control of how the bank is run. The government owns about 30.48% and LIC owns about 30.24% of the bank. This sale is a big deal because together, they currently own almost 95% of the bank. The fact that they're reviewing new bids means the process of selling their stake in the bank is moving forward.
